samples.scenario: Azure Blob Storage container configured with public access enabled, allowing anonymous users to list and read blobs, leading to unauthorized disclosure of sensitive customer information.

technical_data.example_exfiltration_http_request:
GET /customer-data/pii_records.csv HTTP/1.1
Host: storageaccount.blob.core.windows.net
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0
Accept: */*
technical_data.example_list_http_request:
GET /customer-data?restype=container&comp=list HTTP/1.1
Host: storageaccount.blob.core.windows.net
User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
Accept: application/xml

indicators: Container public access level set to "Blob", allowing anonymous read access
Anonymous authenticationType in Azure Activity Logs performing GetBlob and ListBlobs operations
Source IP 203.0.113.45 repeatedly listing and downloading blobs
Storage Analytics logs showing successful 200 responses for anonymous blob retrieval
Unusual access patterns from IPs not in corporate network
samples.detection_method: Audit Azure Blob Storage container public access settings regularly via Azure Policy and Azure Security Center recommendations. Monitor Azure Activity Logs for anonymous authentication types accessing sensitive containers. Enable Storage Analytics logging and parse logs for unexpected ListBlobs and GetBlob operations from unknown IPs. Use automated alerts for changes to container access policies.
relevant_mitre_techniques: T1530 - Data from Cloud Storage Object
T1552.001 - Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
T1560.001 - Archive Collected Data: Archive via Compression

samples.scenario: Google Cloud Storage (GCS) bucket mistakenly configured with 'allUsers' granted 'roles/storage.objectViewer' role, enabling anyone on the internet to download sensitive internal project files.

technical_data.example_exfiltration_http_request:
GET /internal-project-data/roadmap_2024.pdf HTTP/1.1
Host: storage.googleapis.com
User-Agent: wget/1.20.3
Accept: */*
technical_data.example_list_http_request:
GET /storage/v1/b/internal-project-data/o HTTP/1.1
Host: storage.googleapis.com
User-Agent: google-cloud-sdk
Accept: application/json

indicators: IAM policy includes 'allUsers' member with roles/storage.objectViewer role
Audit logs show anonymous principalEmail accessing objects.get and objects.list
Repeated anonymous downloads of sensitive files from IP addresses outside organization
GCS access logs confirming successful HTTP 200 responses for anonymous GET requests
Unusual object listing activity from anonymous users
samples.detection_method: Regularly review GCS bucket IAM policies to detect presence of 'allUsers' or 'allAuthenticatedUsers' with read or write roles. Enable and analyze Cloud Audit Logs for anonymous or unexpected users performing storage.objects.get and storage.objects.list calls. Use Google Cloud Security Command Center to identify publicly accessible buckets. Automate alerts on policy changes granting public access.

Host: companydata.blob.core.windows.net
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0

Analyze logs for repeated downloads from anonymous IPs and unexpected file types indicative of sensitive data exposure.

samples.scenario: Google Cloud Storage bucket configured with overly permissive IAM policy granting allUsers the roles/storage.objectViewer and roles/storage.objectCreator roles, enabling anonymous users to read and write objects, potentially leading to data theft and tampering.

technical_data.example_http_request:
GET /storage/v1/b/secret-project-data/o/credentials.json?alt=media HTTP/1.1
Host: storage.googleapis.com
User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
Accept: application/json

indicators: IAM policy bindings granting 'allUsers' roles/storage.objectViewer and roles/storage.objectCreator
Audit logs showing anonymous principalEmail performing storage.objects.get and storage.objects.insert
Source IP 192.0.2.88 repeatedly accessing and uploading objects
Unusual object insertions such as 'malicious_payload.js' in sensitive buckets
Successful GET requests for sensitive credential files with HTTP 200 status
samples.detection_method: Regularly audit IAM policies for Google Cloud Storage buckets to detect public access granted to 'allUsers' or 'allAuthenticatedUsers'. Analyze Cloud Audit Logs for anonymous or unexpected principalEmail usage performing object read and write operations. Enable bucket-level logging and monitor for anomalous object creation events. Implement alerting for newly uploaded files with suspicious extensions in sensitive buckets.
